# Munder Difflin ### Coolest app to use agents Use the subscriptions you already pay for to run an office of AI agents on your own computer.
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and more. Free and open source.

## What it is Munder Difflin is a desktop app that runs a team of AI agents as an office you can watch. You hire agents, give each one a role, a face and a model, and hand them work in plain words: research, writing, analysis, planning, support, operations, and code too. They plan it, do it and report back. - **Your subscriptions.** Each agent runs the real CLI you already use, signed in with your own plan. We do not sell model access. - **Your computer.** Agents, memory and tasks are plain files in a folder you choose. Open them, back them up or delete them. - **One person to talk to.** Michael, the orchestrator, takes your request and hands each piece to the right agent. This repository is **Munder Difflin Classic**, MIT licensed. Releases ship as source code: you build the app yourself (it takes a few minutes, see [Build from source](#build-from-source)). ## Engines Twelve engines work side by side in one office, plus any command of your own. Each agent picks its own, so one office can mix them.

Claude Code Codex Gemini CLI Antigravity Grok Kimi Code Qwen OpenCode Crush Pi GitHub Copilot Cursor + any custom command

API keys and local models (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) go in **Settings → Agents & Models**. A missing CLI shows as a card in the agent's terminal: **Install** runs the installer, you sign in inside the app, and the agent starts. ## How the office works ``` you ──► Michael (orchestrator) ──► assigns · routes · asks you only when it matters │ ┌───────────┼───────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ agent A ◄──► agent B ◄──► agent C each: a real CLI process + memory + mailbox └───────────┴───────────┘ shared hive: memory · mailboxes · task board · event log (plain files, local git) ``` 1. **Every agent is a real terminal process** (`node-pty`, shown with xterm.js) with its own folder, memory and mailbox, and a character at a desk on the floor. 2. **Agents talk through the hive**, a local git repository of plain files. An agent writes to its `outbox/`, the app delivers to the recipient's `inbox/`, and only the app commits. 3. **Michael runs the floor.** He handles routine requests himself and puts anything that needs you (spend, deletions, a change of scope) in **Ask me**. 4. **Guard rails.** A circuit breaker watches every agent for loops, error storms and runaway spend, and you can set a token cap for each agent. The full design is in [`HIVE.md`](./HIVE.md), [`SPEC.md`](./SPEC.md) and [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## What's in the box | | | |---|---| | | | | **Hire in a few clicks.** Name, role, engine and model, or start from a briefing template. | **Command Center.** The office's task board, next to Michael's terminal, Ask me, triggers, memory and skills. | | | | | **Settings.** Prerequisites shows each engine and whether it is ready; keys, integrations and MCP servers sit beside it. | | - **Memory.** Every agent keeps what it learns, and the whole office shares one memory you can search. - **Schedules and webhooks.** Triggers start work on their own, on a schedule or when a service calls in. - **Slack.** Send work from a thread and the answer comes back in the same thread. - **Keys and integrations.** Save a key once in Settings and give it to the agents that need it. - **MCP servers and skills.** Add tools to an agent from the catalog or by hand. - **Files, editor and git.** Browse and edit each agent's folder, and see its history. ## Build from source You need: - macOS 12+, Windows 10/11 or a modern Linux desktop - **Node 22** (Node 20 works too; Node 26 cannot run the native rebuild). `nvm use` reads `.nvmrc`. - A C/C++ toolchain for `node-pty`: `xcode-select --install` on macOS, Build Tools on Windows - At least one engine CLI from the list above, signed in ```bash git clone https://github.com/HarnessMD/munder-difflin.git cd munder-difflin nvm use npm install # rebuilds node-pty for Electron npm run dev # starts the app ``` The first run walks you through setup, then you land on the floor with Michael at his desk. To make an app you can keep: `npm run dist` (current OS), or `dist:mac`, `dist:win`, `dist:linux`. The result is not signed, so macOS may ask you to right click it and choose **Open**, and Windows may ask you to choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. When a newer release is out, the app tells you; pull the new tag and run the same steps. Other scripts: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run preview`. ## Contributing Start with [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Keep `npm run typecheck` green and build new UI from the tokens in [`DESIGN.md`](./DESIGN.md). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Every pull request shows a before and an after**: screenshots, or a recording when something > moves, under `### Before` and `### After` in the PR template. A PR without them does not merge. > See [Evidence is mandatory](./CONTRIBUTING.md#evidence-is-mandatory). Small, self contained work is in [`good first issue`](https://github.com/HarnessMD/munder-difflin/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22). Questions, bugs or your own office: [Discord](https://discord.gg/SEDzP5ZPk5). Everyone whose code is in Munder Difflin is listed in [`CONTRIBUTORS.md`](./CONTRIBUTORS.md). ## Telemetry A build sends anonymous usage counts (app opened, agent added, feature used) only when it was built with an analytics key. A build from this repository has no key and sends nothing. Never prompts, files or agent output. Details in [`TELEMETRY.md`](./TELEMETRY.md). ## Munder Difflin Pro A paid edition with more, which is not open source, is at [munderdiffl.in](https://munderdiffl.in). ## License The **source code** is [MIT](./LICENSE). The bundled pixel art is **Modern Interiors - RPG Tileset [16X16]** by [LimeZu](https://limezu.itch.io/moderninteriors), used under its Complete Version licence, which **requires credit to LimeZu**; it is carved out of the MIT grant in [`LICENSE-ASSETS`](./LICENSE-ASSETS). The Office cast is drawn in code (`portraitArt.ts`), not LimeZu art. See [`ATTRIBUTION.md`](./src/renderer/src/assets/ATTRIBUTION.md). *Munder Difflin* is a parody and is not affiliated with NBC's *The Office* or Dunder Mifflin. ## Acknowledgements - [LimeZu](https://limezu.itch.io/) for the *Modern Interiors* tilesets. - [`shahar061/the-office`](https://github.com/shahar061/the-office) for the office tileset and map vendoring. - [Pixi.js](https://pixijs.com/), [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org/), [node-pty](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty), [electron-vite](https://electron-vite.org/) and [CodeMirror](https://codemirror.net/). - *The Office* (US), for Munder Difflin, Inc.

Use the subscriptions you already pay for to run an office of AI agents on your own computer.
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and more. Free and open source.

What it is

Munder Difflin is a desktop app that runs a team of AI agents as an office you can watch. You hire agents, give each one a role, a face and a model, and hand them work in plain words: research, writing, analysis, planning, support, operations, and code too. They plan it, do it and report back.

  • Your subscriptions. Each agent runs the real CLI you already use, signed in with your own plan. We do not sell model access.
  • Your computer. Agents, memory and tasks are plain files in a folder you choose. Open them, back them up or delete them.
  • One person to talk to. Michael, the orchestrator, takes your request and hands each piece to the right agent.

This repository is Munder Difflin Classic, MIT licensed. Releases ship as source code: you build the app yourself (it takes a few minutes, see Build from source).

Twelve engines work side by side in one office, plus any command of your own. Each agent picks its own, so one office can mix them.

Claude Code Codex Gemini CLI Antigravity Grok Kimi Code Qwen OpenCode Crush Pi GitHub Copilot Cursor + any custom command

API keys and local models (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) go in Settings → Agents & Models. A missing CLI shows as a card in the agent's terminal: Install runs the installer, you sign in inside the app, and the agent starts.

How the office works

  you ──►  Michael (orchestrator)  ──► assigns · routes · asks you only when it matters
                    │
        ┌───────────┼───────────┐
        ▼           ▼           ▼
     agent A ◄──► agent B ◄──► agent C      each: a real CLI process + memory + mailbox
        └───────────┴───────────┘
   shared hive: memory · mailboxes · task board · event log   (plain files, local git)
  1. Every agent is a real terminal process (node-pty, shown with xterm.js) with its own folder, memory and mailbox, and a character at a desk on the floor.
  2. Agents talk through the hive, a local git repository of plain files. An agent writes to its outbox/, the app delivers to the recipient's inbox/, and only the app commits.
  3. Michael runs the floor. He handles routine requests himself and puts anything that needs you (spend, deletions, a change of scope) in Ask me.
  4. Guard rails. A circuit breaker watches every agent for loops, error storms and runaway spend, and you can set a token cap for each agent.

The full design is in HIVE.md, SPEC.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

What's in the box
Hire in a few clicks. Name, role, engine and model, or start from a briefing template. Command Center. The office's task board, next to Michael's terminal, Ask me, triggers, memory and skills.
Settings. Prerequisites shows each engine and whether it is ready; keys, integrations and MCP servers sit beside it.
  • Memory. Every agent keeps what it learns, and the whole office shares one memory you can search.
  • Schedules and webhooks. Triggers start work on their own, on a schedule or when a service calls in.
  • Slack. Send work from a thread and the answer comes back in the same thread.
  • Keys and integrations. Save a key once in Settings and give it to the agents that need it.
  • MCP servers and skills. Add tools to an agent from the catalog or by hand.
  • Files, editor and git. Browse and edit each agent's folder, and see its history.

Build from source

You need:

  • macOS 12+, Windows 10/11 or a modern Linux desktop
  • Node 22 (Node 20 works too; Node 26 cannot run the native rebuild). nvm use reads .nvmrc.
  • A C/C++ toolchain for node-pty: xcode-select --install on macOS, Build Tools on Windows
  • At least one engine CLI from the list above, signed in
git clone https://github.com/HarnessMD/munder-difflin.git
cd munder-difflin
nvm use
npm install        # rebuilds node-pty for Electron
npm run dev        # starts the app

The first run walks you through setup, then you land on the floor with Michael at his desk.

To make an app you can keep: npm run dist (current OS), or dist:mac, dist:win, dist:linux. The result is not signed, so macOS may ask you to right click it and choose Open, and Windows may ask you to choose More info, then Run anyway. When a newer release is out, the app tells you; pull the new tag and run the same steps.

Other scripts: npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run preview.

Contributing

Start with CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep npm run typecheck green and build new UI from the tokens in DESIGN.md.

Important

Every pull request shows a before and an after: screenshots, or a recording when something moves, under ### Before and ### After in the PR template. A PR without them does not merge. See Evidence is mandatory.

Small, self contained work is in good first issue. Questions, bugs or your own office: Discord. Everyone whose code is in Munder Difflin is listed in CONTRIBUTORS.md.

Telemetry

A build sends anonymous usage counts (app opened, agent added, feature used) only when it was built with an analytics key. A build from this repository has no key and sends nothing. Never prompts, files or agent output. Details in TELEMETRY.md.

Munder Difflin Pro

A paid edition with more, which is not open source, is at munderdiffl.in.

License

The source code is MIT. The bundled pixel art is Modern Interiors - RPG Tileset [16X16] by LimeZu, used under its Complete Version licence, which requires credit to LimeZu; it is carved out of the MIT grant in LICENSE-ASSETS. The Office cast is drawn in code (portraitArt.ts), not LimeZu art. See ATTRIBUTION.md.

Munder Difflin is a parody and is not affiliated with NBC's The Office or Dunder Mifflin.

releases.name: v0.5.5
releases.body:
Munder Difflin 0.5.5.

- **A faster, steadier office.** No freeze at launch, and a busy floor stays smooth.
- **Stop and Archive keep your work.** Archived agents stay archived, and Reopen brings them back.
- **Dictation lands at your cursor**, in the message box, a field or the agent's terminal.
- **A second dictation model**, whisper large-v3-turbo, one download away.
- **Claude Sonnet 5.5** in the model picker.
- **Agents manage Automations**, and every agent reaches your integrations.
- **Detach the IDE** into its own window.
- **A Halloween office**, on by default, with a switch in Settings, General.
- **Windows.** Hooks run from a home folder with a space in its path or on a second drive.

Downloads: macOS `.dmg` (universal), Windows `.exe` (installer or portable), Linux `.AppImage`. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets you verify what you downloaded.

This release carries the installers only, not the 0.5.5 source.

releases.name: v0.5.3
releases.body:
Munder Difflin 0.5.3.

- **Dictate into any app.** Hold Option on the Mac and talk.
- **Transcription on your machine.** Whisper ships inside the app.
- **Meetings hear both sides**, You and Them.
- **More than one office at a time.** New Floor runs a second office in parallel.
- **A missing CLI installs and signs in** from the app.
- **One Save in Settings**, and your agents in your order.

Downloads: macOS `.dmg` (universal), Windows `.exe` (installer or portable), Linux `.AppImage`. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets you verify what you downloaded.

This is a binaries-only release: the tag carries the installers, not the 0.5.3 source.

releases.name: v0.5.2
releases.body:
Munder Difflin 0.5.2.

- **Your name reaches your team.** Agents' names travel sealed.
- **"Not receiving" is said to the sender.** On the relay.
- **Who answers.** One setting, Slack and teammates.
- **Requests stop coming back.** Startup waits for the restore.
- **Michael, shorter.** Terminals, memory, and the agents' composer.

Downloads: macOS `.dmg` (universal), Windows `.exe` (installer or portable), Linux `.AppImage`. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lets you verify what you downloaded.

This is a binaries-only release: the tag carries the installers, not the 0.5.2 source.

# Munder Difflin v0.4.5

## What's new in 0.4.5

**The release that fixes the things you trusted and were quietly wrong.** Cost reporting was off
by more than half after a restart, semantic memory never worked on Apple Silicon, and agents
could not talk to each other reliably. All three are fixed. Plus weekday scheduling, clickable
paths everywhere, one editor instead of two, and 23 community pull requests.

- **Costs are reported right.** The telemetry counter reset on every app restart while the
  session id stayed the same, so the floor under reported spend by a wide margin. It is now folded

aiSummary.oneLiner: Multi-agent harness that runs an office of AI coding clones coordinated locally on your machine.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Munder Difflin is a powerful local desktop application that transforms standalone, single-agent CLIs into an organized, collaborative office of AI workers. It effectively wraps existing subscriptions and coding CLIs (such as Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and Pi) into independent, headless workers. A centralized AI clone named Michael serves as the orchestrator, intelligently routing tasks, coordinating communication, and managing a shared memory space. It visualizes this complex system through a dynamic virtual office floor using a React and Pixi.js frontend. Under the hood, it utilizes a highly performant, markdown-first semantic memory layer to ensure instant recall across sessions.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent coordination: Utilizes a master orchestrator agent to intelligently route and assign tasks across multiple specialized worker agents.
Provider wrapping: Seamlessly wraps standard terminal CLIs like Claude Code, Gemini, and GitHub Copilot into fully capable, headless workers.
Local execution: Runs entirely on your own machine using Electron, React, and node-pty to ensure privacy and low latency.
Visualized office floor: Represents active background agents as interactive avatars working dynamically in a shared virtual workspace.
Bring-your-own keys: Leverages user-provided API keys or local LLMs to efficiently bypass centralized subscription constraints.
Instant semantic recall: Maintains a markdown-first memory layer providing agents with immediate access to cross-session knowledge.
Isolated git worktrees: Ensures parallel agents never collide by providing each with optional, isolated git worktrees.

useCases.title: Coordinating complex coding tasks
useCases.description: Breaking down a large repository refactor into smaller tasks and routing them to distinct LLM workers based on their strengths.

useCases.title: Background development
useCases.description: Setting up a persistent team of coding agents to continuously work on feature branches while you are away from the keyboard.

useCases.title: Visualizing AI workflows
useCases.description: Using the Pixi.js avatar interface to graphically monitor which AI provider is actively executing commands in real-time.

useCases.title: Avoiding single-model limits
useCases.description: Distributing workloads across various provider APIs (Claude, Grok, Gemini) to maximize overall hourly rate limits.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers aiming to manage multiple autonomous coding agents simultaneously without relying on expensive, centralized multi-agent cloud platforms. It is tailored for advanced users requiring parallel execution and visual coordination across diverse toolsets.
